Project background

The challenge

Product issue
High bounce rate from landing screen (Fig.1)
User Test Finding
"I don't see what I can do here..." (Search)
Product goal
  • Increase flight search rate
  • Reduce bounce rate
Design challenge
How might we make it easy to tell and discover a future story without writing an entire article?
Key Stage #1

Reframing the problem

Search needed to be obvious, but there're other things needed to be on the page. ↳ How much of the screen should search occupy?

Flight search (primary action by chance)
Help majority of users see where to start right away.
Everything else (secondary by choice)
Leave enough space for post-booking and marketing content.
Key Stage #2

Exploring the trade-off

Option A — Full search
  • Give users the complete search interface immediately
  • Trade-off: Secondary content was pushed below the fold, reducing its visibility
  • Open wireframe
Option B — Minimal search
  • Reduce search to a smaller entry point to preserve more space
  • Trade-off: The reduced UI was less recognizable as a travel search experience
  • Open wireframe
Key Stage #3

Converting the trade-off

Turning it into an interactive crossroads: expanding as the user needed more information

Option C - Expandable search
  • Initial state: communicates the concept of travel search
  • Engaged state: user's action will define path (Typing VS. Scrolling)
Key Stage #4

Final design

Visual design
  • Color distinguishes IA and status of interaction
  • Animation emphasizes visual cue
Interaction sequence
  1. Initial view
  2. Searching: user enters location > search section enpanded
  3. Exploring: user interact other components > moves toward to each path
Open interactive prototype
Learnings

"Design around the user's level of intent."

This project reinforced something I continue to use in my product design work: An interface doesn't always need to show everything at once.

When users are still deciding what to do, clarity can come from showing less. As their intent becomes clearer, the interface can reveal more context and detail.

Probelm area

Product issue
Users abandon the booking path after selecting the flight from the listing
User Test Finding
  • "I already selected what I want. I want to book it while it's available."
  • "I need to check overlay details before select the flight."
Product goal
  • Increase listing - booking page funnel
  • Reduce bounce rate during the booking process
Design challenge
Flight details should be available in the booking path but should not compete with tier 1 context of the pages

Draft solutions

Suggestion
  1. Add flight detail screen as a drawer view - linked from both listing and booking
  2. Rearrange booking input fields - first booking step
Diverge options
Option A
  • Add flight detail screen as a mandatory step: Listing > Details > Booking
Option B
  • Add flight detail screen as an optional step: Listing > Details > Booking
Wireframe and user test
  • 6/10 Users reacted positively with Option B
  • 2/10 Users reacted positively with Option A
  • 2/10 Users reacted neutral
  • Open option B wireframe

Converge and Prototype

Visual design
  • Emphasize critical information (stops, alternate airport, etc.)
  • Clarify the group of information using spacing, background-color
  • Build a card component for consistent section
Visual cues
  • Navigating icon: back vs. close
  • Timeline icon: point a vs. point b
  • Highlighted text: critical information
  • Status code: filled (active) vs empty (inactive)
Open interactive prototype

Hand-off

Interaction flow
  • To visualize user’s interaction flow to help product developers overviewing final UX flow.
  • This helps whole product team to oversee the end-to-end production process.
  • Enlarge image

Project background

Product issue
  • Users are discouraged by the full-blocked dialog modal.
  • The presentation is too aggressive, and the interaction is passive.
User Interview Quote
  • "I felt kicked-out..."
  • "It's shutting me out instead of talking to me..."
Product goal
  • Increase customer retention from the listing
Design challenge
Grab user's attention less aggressively

Draft ideas

Friendly interaction sequence
  • Mimic the 'chat interaction' to present less aggressively
  • Utilize conversational sequence to deliver information actively

Draft interaction

Humanly interaction
  • Utilize persona to make the whole engagement more friendly
  • The conversational sequence would help breakdown the information into two way communication.
  • This format has more room to slip conversion-friendly message.
Less input, more feedback
  • Reducing the input forms would help users to focus.
  • Instead of forcing users to be smart, the feedback logic should improve to deal with corner cases.

Build interactions and prototype

Open interactive prototype
Engaging sequence
  • Green blinking indicates agent online
  • Animating chat UI doesn't require to block out the whole page.
  • The sequence would conclude with a single constructive action.
Feedback sequence
  • Add conditional feedback to simulate conversation
  • The chat is not necessarily stackable to keep the space minimum.
  • Final feedback without previous conversation would give user the sign of 'DONE'.

Contribution

Product strategy
  • Collaborating with product owner to set MVP strategy
UI design
  • Creating a low-fidelity mock for early validation
  • Creating an interactive prototype using Sketch and UXPin
Front-end
  • Prototype the whole interaction with HTML/CSS and JS
  • Implement MVP directly through A/B testing tool
UX design
  • Illustrate the persona to help product to shape the context of interaction
  • Analyze traffic data and user interview result to address the pain points

Onboarding Process
  • Too many steps to go through
  • The onboarding process is generally tasteless

Chatting with a Match
  • Talking some you just met isn’t easy
  • The conversation starter/aid might be useful - e.g., icebreaker

Oversee user's journey

Critical path
  • Map out the overall flow of end-to-end user experience
  • Use this to see the cause and effect flow in the step by step process
  • Make sure those new ideas aligned with the final goal of users

Converge solutions

  • Utilize chatting method

  • Direct feedback
  • Conversational interaction
  • Share the taste of astrology aspect

node.html:
Product background

The challenge

Product issue
As Upward doubles down on marriage-focused dating, it needs a way for users to express and assess long-term compatibility.
User Test Finding
"I hate when I'm talking to someone and find out we want something completely different..."
Product goal
Help users express their vision for the future and discover where it aligns with others'.
Design challenge
How might we help users express and explore their vision for the future without writing an essay?
Key Stage #1

Exploring: Making the abstract tangible

Metaphor-driven
Borrow familiar real-world metaphors, like building blocks, to make an abstract future feel tangible.
Narrative-driven
Turn utilitarian forms into a visual story, bringing choices about marriage, family, home, and traditions to life.
Key Stage #2

Testing: How users would tell their story

Option A — 'Future Storybook'
  • A playful, illustrated experience that evolves as users make choices.
  • Pros: Emotionally engaging; makes serious topics feel approachable.
  • Cons: May make information harder to scan on someone else's profile.
Option B — 'Structured Future Profile'
  • A structured, text-based experience designed for clarity and efficiency.
  • Pros: Easy to scan and compare at a glance.
  • Cons: Feels like filling out a job application.
Key Stage #3

Visualizing: How to bring the story to life

01. Toy-Inspired Building Blocks
  • A playful building-block aesthetic.
  • Risk: Potential copyright concerns.
02. Retro Illustration
  • A nostalgic illustration style aligned with the new brand.
  • Risk: Could reinforce stereotypes.
03. Boutique Stickers
  • A sticker-based visual language aligned with the existing style.
  • Risk: Could limit the range of stories expressed.
Key Stage #4

Final design: A refined retro aesthetic

The result: a two-part experience — build your vision, then discover someone else's.

PART A — STORYTELLING EXPERIENCE
  • Express your future
  • Make envisioning the future feel approachable and personal.
  • Integrates into the onboarding flow.
PART A — STORYTELLING EXPERIENCE
  • Discover someone else's
  • Make another person's vision easy to understand at a glance.
  • Integrates into the discover flow.
Learnings

"It's not how long it takes, but how it feels."

Visual storytelling can make abstract ideas easier to understand and discuss. But the experience should never make a personal vision feel like a contract.

The best design provides enough structure to communicate what matters while leaving room for nuance.

frontmatter.title: Future Vision
frontmatter.excerpt: Helping people express the future they envision—and discover whether it aligns with someone else's.

node.html:
Project background

The challenge

Product issue
Map discovery gave users freedom but lacked a clear starting point, leading to low engagement.
Product goal
Increase profile views and engagement by helping users discover relevant people more easily.
Design challenge
How might we guide users toward meaningful connections without taking away their freedom to explore?
Key Stage #1

Exploring: Finding direction in an open map

Explore why an open map can feel aimless, and how clearer starting points and contextual cues could help.

  • Too many or too few people nearby.
  • Little context beyond a single photo.
  • Often the same people users saw yesterday.
Option 1. Browsing feed
  • Curated profiles ordered by proximity.
  • Key profile information and actionable buttons at a glance.
Option 2. Focused browsable carousel
  • Curated profiles ordered by proximity.
  • Profile highlight with full-profile access
Option 3. Zoomed-In 3D Navigation
  • Zoom in on one profile at a time.
  • Explore a heads-up display (HUD) for profile highlights.
Key Stage #2

Re-routing: Measuring focus and freedom

Reduce distractions without sacrificing the freedom to explore. ↳ Introduce a hybrid map discovery model with Focus Mode.

Focuse mode
One proflie at a time: A focused discovery flow with actionable profile previews.
Exit anytime
Stay in control: Users can leave the focused flow and continue exploring map freely.
Key Stage #3

Re-targeting: Tuning the goal-oriented UX

Go deep to connect, or go wide to explore - one at a time.

Focus mode layout option
  • Option A — Photo-First: Prioritize profile photos and compatibility signals.
  • Option B — Editorial: Prioritize profile content through an editorial layout.
Key Stage #4

Final design: Focus Mode with the freedom to exit

Learnings

"Have options, not distractions"

More options without mindful guadience, are distraction. The key is to give users enough direction to take the next step, while keeping them in control of where they go.

Good discovery isn't about showing users everything. It's about helping them find what matters to them.

frontmatter.title: Guided Discover over the Map
frontmatter.excerpt: Making map discover experience more guided, relevant, and engaging.
